labels.notes: Unmarked and proposed 'partial (a reading)'. That is right. Every clause of Def 2.13 is carried, and I checked the elaborated structure with #print. (i) Gamma is jointly continuous on [0,1]^2: ContinuousOn (uncurry Gamma) (Icc 0 1 x Icc 0 1) (:123). (ii) Every slice Gamma t, t in [0,1], is a future chronal curve of W over [0,1] (:124). (iii) The endpoints are fixed at gamma0 0 and gamma0 1 (:125-126). (iv) Gamma 0 = gamma0 and Gamma 1 = gamma1 on [0,1] (:127-128). The premise of (1), two future curves with the same endpoints, follows from the existence of Gamma (chronalCurveOn_left/right, right_zero/one), so ChronallyHomotopicOn := exists Gamma is equivalent to 'premise and exists Gamma'. FutureOneConnectedOn (:139) quantifies over all p, q and all pairs of future chronal curves of W over [0,1] from p to q, as (2) does. FutureOneConnected is W = top, which is Sbierski's M. The hypothesis '(M,g) time-oriented Lorentzian with a continuous metric' is weakened to any causality on any topological space. The one reading is Sbierski's piecewise smooth future timelike curve (Def 2.1-2.2, :235-246) read as a future chronal curve. That is the binder's reading in row schwdef:timelike_curve (binder.toml:146), and it has no OQ/DEC row. OQ-114 (DECISIONS.md:337, OPEN) concerns Def 2.12's Cauchy hypersurfaces only and does not bear on Def 2.13. The disclosure that this is 'not literally >= Sbierski's Lorentzian notion' is accurate. Under the C0 causality, where ≪_U is defined by Sbierski's curves in U, every piecewise smooth timelike curve is chronal: continuity gives a parameter neighbourhood inside any open N containing c(t), and the sub-arc witnesses ≪_N. The converse fails, since chronal curves need not be piecewise smooth. So the ETT for-all ranges over more curves and the ETT exists admits more homotopies, and the two notions are a priori incomparable. The module states this in '## The reading' (:61-67), not under '## SCOPE (disclosed)'; see finding 2. Non-vacuity: the hypotheses of FutureOneConnectedOn are satisfiable, and timelikeLine_chronallyHomotopicOn_sq relates id and s^2, two distinct chronal curves of the timelike line, through a homotopy that is non-constant in t. The joint continuity carries weight, because the step homotopies are excluded. Mathematically the notion is not trivially true either: on a narrow 1+1 Minkowski cylinder two chronal curves with different winding numbers admit no continuous homotopy rel endpoints at all. No such separation is in Lean, as SCOPE discloses (:101).

It formalizes ETT.tex prop:GX_espace_temps_topo for an abstract (G,X)-structure whose model X is a type variable with an arbitrary Causality, and it defines chartSource, chartImage and ChartIso (:73-85) for any OpenPartialHomeomorph, with no concrete model. Its docstring (:108-111) avoids Causal.Remarks.MassiveManifold on purpose, 'which reaches a model'. No metric notion appears: no Lorentzian metric, length or geodesic in any statement. Faithfulness to Def 2.13. I read InexSchwarzschild2.tex:370-390 and Defs 2.1-2.2 (:235-246) against the structure fields; see the label notes. Joint continuity is also what the consumers need: the openness of I in Thm 3.1 Step 3 (:621) and of J in Thm 4.11 (:1623) is a tube-lemma argument on [0,1]^2.

Paper findings, Step 2.1 (:567-584). Concatenation splits at s = 1/2 (:572), and Gamma(t,s) = (sigma_{lambda(t)} * lambda|[t,1])(s) with lambda(0) = 0 (:575-579). At t = 0, sigma_{lambda(0)} = sigma_0 ≡ 0, so Gamma(0,.) is 0 on [0,1/2] and lambda(2s-1) after. That is neither lambda nor timelike: the tangent vanishes on [0,1/2] (Def 2.1). At t = 1, lambda|[1,1] is a point, so Gamma(1,.) is sigma_{lambda(1)}(2s) and then constant: neither sigma_{lambda(1)} nor timelike. Confirmed. Gamma is jointly continuous on [0,1]^2, and the slices with t in (0,1) are timelike (a segment to lambda(t) ≫ 0, then lambda, both one-sided tangents future timelike), so the defect is confined to the two end slices. The proposed fix is Gamma(t,s) = sigma_{lambda(t)}(s/t) on [0,t], lambda(s) on [t,1], for t in (0,1], and Gamma(0,.) = lambda. I verified it: Gamma(1,.) = sigma_{lambda(1)}. The endpoints are 0 and lambda(1) for every t. Each slice is piecewise smooth with future timelike one-sided tangents at s = t, namely lambda(t)/t and lambda'(t+). Continuity at t -> 0 holds because |(s/t) lambda(t)| <= |lambda(t)| -> 0 and lambda(s) -> 0 for s <= t. Continuity elsewhere follows by gluing two closed pieces that agree at s = t.

Paper findings, notational. At :876 Prop 4.12's proof takes gamma_i : [t0,t1] -> M_ext but writes gamma0(0) = gamma1(0) and gamma0(1) = gamma1(1), which should be t0 and t1. It also writes Gamma : [t0,t1] x [t0,t1], where :867 and :872 use [0,1] x [t0,t1]. Confirmed. At :1623, sigma : [y0^-, s] -> M_int is 'from gamma(x0^-)', but the homotopy is between gamma|[y0^-,s] and sigma with fixed endpoints, and (FuturePastPreserving) (:1616-1617) is about I^+(gamma(y0^-)). So x0^- stands for y0^-. Confirmed. x0^- = -3/4 epsilon is a real symbol of the proof (Step 1.2, :1606; Step 1.5, :1772, :1790), so this is a wrong symbol, not an undefined one. Both slips are harmless.

Equivalence, dual and iso statements, read in the source and confirmed with #check. chronallyHomotopicOn_equivalence is an Equivalence on {gamma // C.ChronalCurveOn W gamma 0 1}. ChronalHomotopyOn.dual maps C to C.dual with the curve parameter reversed. dual_symm reverses both parameters. dual_futureOneConnectedOn : C.dual.FutureOneConnectedOn W <-> C.FutureOneConnectedOn W is an iff with C.dual. The IsCausalIso forms (:494-538) take e : M ≃ₜ N and e.opensCongr W. The ChartIso forms (:558-647) are stated for the library's Causal.ChartIso (GXStructure.lean:82) with W <= chartSource e and chartImage e W. The MapsTo hypotheses of ChartIso.chronallyHomotopicOn_iff are needed for <= and are implied by the left side in =>, so nothing is lost. futureOneConnectedOn_congr_lt is an iff for two causalities with the same ≪_U on every U.

findings.what: The checklist row for 'future directed timelike curves' reads '✓ carried, read as future chronal curves'. The module (:65-67) and REPORT both say the ETT class is strictly larger and the two notions of future one-connectedness are a priori incomparable, which is a reading, not a carried hypothesis. The disclosure is accurate but sits in '## The reading', not in '## SCOPE (disclosed)', which kb/0006 reserves for 'what is ... proved in a reading'.
findings.fix: Mark the row '⚠ reading (C0 layer 3)'. Add a SCOPE bullet: Sbierski's piecewise smooth timelike curves are replaced by chronal curves (binder row schwdef:timelike_curve). Under the C0 model the ETT class is larger, so neither notion of future one-connectedness implies the other at layer 1, and the row is partial.

findings.what: Stranded-lemma concern (kb/0047). The two lemmas are general ChartIso facts of the ETT layer, now sitting in a homotopy module. chronalCurveOn_symm_image is the C.lt instance of the generic-relation Causal.ChartIso.curveOn_symm (Remarks/MassiveManifold.lean:113, model layer). It also duplicates Causal.Flat.curveOn_chart_symm (Flat/CauchyComplete.lean:2516, model layer), which REPORT does not mention. The forward lemma has no counterpart anywhere. Their natural home is Causal.GXStructure, beside ChartIso, chartSource and chartImage.

findings.what: Precision of the Step 2.1 finding, which may go to the author. The finding is correct, and so is the fix (verified). The Lean anchor timelikeLine_not_chronalCurveOn_pause, however, covers only the t = 0 slice, and only on the 1-dimensional timelike line. Sbierski's manifolds have dimension d+1 >= 2 (:228), so the lemma is an analogue, not an instance. The t = 1 slice and the (d+1)-dimensional case are argued in prose. The docstring's 'the 1 + 0-dimensional Minkowski space' does not flag this.
findings.fix: In the findings row, cite the failure directly against Def 2.1 (:236: the tangent vanishes on [0,1/2] at t = 0 and on [1/2,1] at t = 1) and Def 2.13 (:383: Gamma(0,.) = lambda, Gamma(1,.) = sigma_{lambda(1)}). Present the Lean lemma as a 1-dimensional illustration, together with ChronalCurveOn.injOn, which applies in Minkowski space through irreflexivity of ≪, a model fact. Add that the interior slices are timelike and Gamma is jointly continuous, so the defect is a slip in the end slices. Optionally say 'a 1-dimensional analogue (Sbierski assumes d+1 >= 2, :228)' in the docstring.

notes: Verdict minor: no major finding. Faithful and correctly unmarked; the closer's proposed status is 'partial (a reading)'. The build is clean under -DwarningAsError=true, with 0 sorry and standard axioms on all 57 declarations. The ETT layer holds: 29-module closure, no model, and GXStructure and CausalIsoInvariance are model-free. Both paper findings are true, and the Step 2.1 fix is correct. The scope is respected, and there are no name clashes. The Step 2.1 finding also bears on the evidence of T-loc-minkowski-future-one-connected (programme/roadmap.toml:2187), which quotes the printed formula as the homotopy to formalize. That target should use the corrected split at s = t or the convex combination it already proposes. The probe AuditProbe1.lean was written under this campaign directory and deleted.
